title: test_cipher.rs: AES ECB/CBC/CTR/OFB via cipher traits
description:
Write tests/test_cipher.rs: test cipher::* impls for AES ECB/CBC/CTR/OFB against NIST SP 800-38A Appendix F vectors.

## What
Verify that AES cipher type parameters (KeySize, IvSize, BlockSize) are correct and encrypt/decrypt output is byte-exact NIST.

## Algorithm
1. Load vectors from testvectors/nist/aes_38a.rs (compiled-in constants).
2. ECB (BlockEncrypt/Decrypt):
   a. use cipher::{BlockEncrypt, KeyInit}; let cipher = Aes128Ecb::new_from_slice(key).unwrap();
   b. let mut block = GenericArray::clone_from_slice(pt_block);
   c. cipher.encrypt_block(&mut block); assert_eq!(block.as_slice(), ct_block);
   d. Repeat for AES-192, AES-256. Repeat decrypt direction.
3. CBC (BlockEncrypt + cbc::Encryptor):
   a. use cipher::{KeyIvInit, BlockEncryptMut}; let enc = CbcEncryptor::new_from_slices(key, iv).unwrap();
   b. encrypt 4 blocks; assert byte-exact against NIST F.2.
4. CTR (StreamCipher):
   a. use cipher::{KeyIvInit, StreamCipher}; let mut ctr = Aes128Ctr::new_from_slices(key, iv).unwrap();
   b. apply_keystream on plaintext copy; assert_eq against NIST F.5.
5. OFB (StreamCipher):
   a. Same pattern as CTR using Aes128Ofb; NIST F.4 vectors.
6. Compile-time trait check: fn _block_enc<C: cipher::BlockEncrypt>() {} for ECB types.

## Defensive rules
- Use GenericArray::clone_from_slice (not unsafe pointer casts) for block construction
- Assert block size at compile time via cipher::BlockSizeUser::BlockSize == U16
- Never use the wolfssl-wolfcrypt AES C FFI directly; always go through the cipher trait
- If cfg flag aes_cbc/aes_ctr/aes_ofb is not emitted by build.rs, tests for those modes will fail to compile; document in #[cfg_attr] comments

## Agent team
- Agent R: read aes.rs to confirm type names for each mode and which cfg flags gate them; read build.rs to understand how cfg flags are emitted
- Agent I: write test_cipher.rs per algorithm above
- Agent T: independently transcribe NIST SP 800-38A F.1.1 (AES-128 ECB encrypt, first block) from the NIST PDF; confirm it matches the aes_38a.rs constant

- AES-128-CBC F.2.1: iv=000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f, first block ct=7649abac8119b246cee98e9b12e9197d
